title: Japa Interview
summary: KC prepares an honest portfolio for the fictional Open Window creative fellowship, checks three interview answers and keeps a follow-up opportunity open. Practice and callback routes preserve the same opportunity; private wedding sources stay protected.

protect.text: Ngozi: Our private-first checks do not stop you making plans for yourself. Just keep other people's accounts private.
protect.summary: The private-first pact supports KC's own opportunity while preserving other people's accounts.

public_case.text: Ngozi: A public case and your own future both need work you can explain. Neither needs somebody else's private account as a shortcut.
public_case.summary: The public-case pact does not replace consent or KC's own creative choices.

stages.title: An open window. A closed microphone.
stages.text:
KC receives an interview invitation from Open Window, an invented creative fellowship.
Tunde: Is the window open because the fan is broken?
KC: It is a metaphor.
Ngozi: Then you can close it when the rain starts.

Read the portfolio brief before promising anything.
stages.summary: Read the fictional creative-fellowship brief. This chapter keeps an opportunity open; it does not decide whether KC leaves.

records.title: Open Window · OW-12
lines: Creative fellowship: short nonfiction studies
Bring work you can credit and explain
Private sources require specific permission before showing
Interview and follow-up are story appointments

choices.label: Read the brief and prepare work I can explain
Promise footage and skills without checking either
choices.hint: Start with the brief. KC can make a strong application without promising work or permission he does not have.

stages.title: The credits need more than one name
stages.text:
KC: I filmed the wedding.
Ngozi: You did not cook it, serve it and carry every chair.
KC: My tripod carried a great deal emotionally.

Separate your filming and editing from the crew's work. The source notes are the basis for the three interview questions.
stages.summary: Credit KC for filming/editing and the crew for their own work. Do not claim sole authorship of the event.

records.title: Contribution notes
lines: KC: filming and editing
Catering team: preparation and service
Other crew: their own event roles
An event recording is not sole authorship of the event

choices.label: Describe my filming/editing and credit the crew's work
Claim I delivered the entire wedding alone
choices.hint: Use the contribution notes. Credit the work KC did and the work other people did.

stages.title: Keep the source behind the claim
stages.text:
The private original and earlier crop remain separate.
KC: One version got attention. The other keeps answering questions.

Keep the retained original and editing history available for comparison. Keeping a source does not give permission to show everyone in it. If a stored source is missing, the journal can restore earned records.
stages.summary: Keep the original and editing history for private comparison. Restore an earned missing source through the journal; do not replace it with the crop.

records.title: Source notes
lines: Private original retained
Earlier crop retained as an editing record
Helping action omitted by the earlier crop
Showing a person still needs permission for that use

choices.label: Retain the original, crop and editing history separately
Discard the original because the crop is easier to explain
choices.hint: Preserve the original and the editing record. An easier headline is not a replacement source.

stages.title: A frame has edges. So does a claim.
stages.text:
Ngozi: What happened outside the frame?
KC: I have a theory.
Ngozi: We have met your theories. Bring the source notes.

The visible helping action matters. It still does not establish every off-frame event or another person's motive.
stages.summary: Limit the claim to what the source shows and mark the gaps for comparison.

records.title: Scope notes
lines: Visible action can be described
Off-frame events still need checking
A motive is not established by a crop
The family investigation remains separate from the fellowship

choices.label: Describe the visible action and mark the off-frame gaps
Use the frame to claim every event and motive is settled
choices.hint: Keep the claim within the frame and the source notes. Off-frame events and motives still need checking.

stages.title: Three questions before the call
stages.text:
Use the contribution, source and scope notes to build three consistent answers. The board keeps each selection. A presentation needing correction offers free practice or a later callback; neither closes the opportunity.

Tunde: I can be your interviewer.
KC: Ask about my work.
Tunde: When will it pay for the Wi-Fi?
stages.summary: Select consistent answers about your contribution, retained original and the limits of the frame, then review. Guided answers, practice and callback are equivalent routes.

choices.label: Continue with the checked answers

first.text:
Interviewer: Your notes are consistent. Let us talk about the work.
KC: My first presentation has survived its own introduction.
first.summary: The first checked presentation continues into the same interview.

practice.text:
Interviewer: The practice notes are clearer. A correction is useful work too.
KC: My second draft has stopped claiming it cooked rice.
practice.summary: The corrected practice presentation continues without a reduced opportunity.

callback.text:
Interviewer: Thank you for returning with checked notes. We kept this callback open.
KC: The window even has a calendar.
callback.summary: The later callback continues with the same opportunity and checked notes.

stages.title: We would like your authentic voice
stages.text:
Interviewer: We would like your authentic voice.
KC begins answering.
Interviewer: You are muted.
KC: A very authentic problem.

A written prompt shows the same question. Choose the answer from your checked notes; no audio or timed response is required.
stages.summary: Use the written prompt and checked notes. The mute joke never hides a clue or blocks progress.

choices.label: Answer from the checked notes and ask for written clarification if needed
Invent new credits to fill the silence
choices.hint: The checked notes are enough. Use them and ask for the written question rather than inventing work.

stages.title: One permission does not cover the room
stages.text:
The MC has agreed to a short excerpt of his own solo introduction for this private fellowship review. That agreement covers the MC alone and this review. It does not cover guests, Nneka, the helping action or a later public post.

KC: An approval with edges. I am beginning to recognise the theme.

Keep the full source private and record the limited permission before choosing a portfolio piece.
stages.summary: Record the MC's specific private-review permission for his solo introduction. Keep everyone else and the full source private.

records.title: MC's review permission
lines: Subject: MC's solo introduction only
Use: private Open Window portfolio review
Other people and helping action: excluded
Later public post: not covered
Full original: retained privately

choices.label: Keep the limited permission and exclude everyone it does not cover
Treat the MC's permission as permission for everyone
choices.hint: Permission covers the named person and use. The other people and the full source remain private.

stages.title: Which piece belongs in this review?
stages.text:
Choose the permitted solo-MC excerpt with a clear editing note, or the earlier consenting practice piece. Both are valid. The helping action can be described as an editing lesson without showing or identifying the private participants.

Neither choice deletes the wedding original or closes a later ending.
stages.summary: Use the permitted MC-only excerpt or the consenting practice piece. Keep the original private, credit the work honestly and preserve the same opportunity.

choices.label: Use the approved solo-MC excerpt with a clear editing/context note
Use the consenting practice piece and explain the editing lesson

original_excerpt.text: The portfolio sheet labels the MC introduction as a limited excerpt, not an account of the entire wedding.
original_excerpt.summary: The selected MC-only excerpt is labelled with its limited scope.

practice_piece.text: The portfolio sheet identifies the consenting practice piece. It does not pretend to be the wedding original.
practice_piece.summary: The selected practice piece is honestly identified and keeps the wedding source private.

stages.title: The note stays with the piece
stages.text:
KC writes what he filmed, what he edited and what the selected piece cannot establish. The private helping-action source stays with the family investigation. This portfolio note does not silently settle any unresolved conversation with Ngozi.

Interviewer: That is a clearer explanation than the headline.
KC: It fits less comfortably on a thumbnail.
stages.summary: Keep honest credits and scope with the selected piece. Preserve the family source and any separate unresolved disclosure.

choices.label: Attach the honest credits and scope note
Remove the note so the piece can imply more
choices.hint: Keep the explanation with the piece. The viewer should not have to guess its credits or limits.

stages.title: An option, not a decision made for you
stages.text:
Interviewer: We would like a follow-up conversation about your next piece.
KC: Is this where my life changes in a montage?
Interviewer: This is where we agree another conversation.

Accept the follow-up or ask for time to consider its date. Both keep the creative opportunity available. The decision about leaving remains KC's later choice.
stages.summary: Keep the follow-up open, either by accepting or asking for time. Every presentation route and portfolio piece preserves that option.

choices.label: Keep the follow-up invitation open
Ask for time while keeping the follow-up option

stages.title: Did they ask about the Wi-Fi?
stages.text:
Tunde: Did they ask about the Wi-Fi?
KC: They asked about my work.
Ngozi: And did your work remember everyone else's name?
KC: It has credits now. Proper ones.

Save the opportunity separately from wedding evidence. The journal will keep a note after this chapter; it is not a clue about the bag.
stages.summary: Tell the family about the checked portfolio and keep the follow-up separate from wedding evidence.

choices.label: Keep the opportunity note and the wedding records separate

stages.title: The window stays open
stages.text:
Japa Interview complete. Your checked answers, presentation route, portfolio piece and follow-up choice are saved. KC gains two mastery once. Practice or callback did not reduce the opportunity. The family sources, phone battery and meeting decisions remain as they were.

Tunde's next trip is about to acquire some very persistent passengers. Danfo Chase follows.
stages.summary: KC prepared an honest portfolio and retained the Open Window follow-up. Two KC mastery are awarded once, with no new wedding clue or StreetCoins. Danfo Chase follows.

choices.label: Save the portfolio and follow-up opportunity
